examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratio Using the Pythagorean Identity
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/0e88dc5962fc5bd128c0de5502e8dcd1edf34353de1d31c2d8a21ac672633644.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2},$ what is $\csc\theta?$
examples.worked_solution:
We're given that $x=-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\cos\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\sin\theta\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\cos\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{3}{4}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $\sin\theta$ is negative in the third quadrant. So, $\sin\theta = -\dfrac 1 2.$

Finally, knowing that $\csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta},$ we have

$$
\csc\theta = \dfrac{1}{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} =-2.
$$

feedback.problem: If $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{2}$ and ${180}^{∘}<\theta <{270}^{∘},$ then what is the value of $tan⁡\theta ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/7873579bb5dd1976330ec24f13b30dd384f916cf23bbf48aac4b2a522ee9548a.png)

We're given that $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{2}.$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is negative in the third quadrant. So, $sin⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}{(-\frac{1}{2})}=\sqrt{3}.
$$
